rule: When a provider transfer operator exposes a passthrough config dict (e.g. `extra_config`), apply it last — after every top-level-derived field — so it actually wins for overlapping keys as documented
trigger: A passthrough dict is merged into an API-representation dict before the object is constructed, while top-level params (`schema_fields`, `max_bad_records`) are still assigned onto the constructed object afterwards
rationale: The escape-hatch dict is documented as taking precedence, so applying it early silently lets typed parameters override user overrides for the same field

evidence.excerpt: `extra_config` does not consistently take precedence for overlapping fields

rule: Keep the `deferrable` constructor default as the inline literal `conf.getboolean("operators", "default_deferrable", fallback=False)`; do not switch it to `None` and resolve the config inside the body
trigger: An operator/sensor `__init__` signature changes `deferrable=conf.getboolean("operators", "default_deferrable", fallback=False)` to `deferrable=None` or any other default
rationale: A custom AST pre-commit checker recognises the literal default; changing the shape either silently defeats the checker or forces its logic to become more complicated

evidence.excerpt: should break our ast checker; leave this deferrable thing as it is

rule: Do not add a boolean opt-in flag for behaviour that only changes an operator's return value when existing users read the old value from a separate named XCom key
trigger: New `__init__` boolean parameter (e.g. `return_gcs_uris`) whose only effect is the format of the value returned by `execute()`, while the legacy value is still pushed to its own XCom key
rationale: Operators push named XCom keys independently of the return value, so a return-value-only change is already backwards compatible and the flag adds permanent public API surface for nothing

evidence.excerpt: it shouldn't affect existing users who read from XCom. Is the flag really necessary?

rule: Raise built-in exceptions such as `RuntimeError` for internal/programming errors in provider code instead of `AirflowException`
trigger: New `raise AirflowException(...)` added inside a provider package trigger, hook or operator helper for a state/invariant violation
rationale: Providers are being decoupled from airflow core exception types, so reviewers reject new `AirflowException` usages in provider modules

evidence.excerpt: Let's not use AirflowException

rule: Log transient, retried API errors inside a trigger's async polling loop at info/debug level, or rate-limit them; do not emit a warning on every retry
trigger: `except <TransientError>` inside a trigger `run()` loop calls `self.log.warning(...)` immediately before `await asyncio.sleep(self.polling_period_seconds)`
rationale: Triggers poll continuously in a shared triggerer process, so one warning per retry floods the deployment's logs for the entire duration of a provider outage

evidence.excerpt: Logging a warning on every transient 503 can generate high-volume warning logs

rule: In a trigger, filter the result of a bulk list call that is already in scope rather than issuing one API request per item
trigger: A comprehension inside a trigger awaits `self.hook.get_<resource>(name=...)` once per name when a `list_<resources>()` result for the same namespace/label selector was already awaited
rationale: All triggers share a single event loop in the triggerer, so per-item API calls multiply latency and API quota consumption for every deferred task

evidence.excerpt: Why are you doing an API call for every pod when you called `list_pods` already

rule: When a trigger waits on state that only becomes true eventually (a pod reaching Succeeded, a job finishing), poll in a bounded `while` loop with a timeout instead of a single check plus a stale fallback
trigger: Trigger code performs one list/get call and then does `if not <resource>:` to fall back to a previously captured list rather than re-polling until the condition holds or a timeout expires
rationale: A query issued too early can run before the resource settles, so the fallback silently returns the wrong object — e.g. missing the replacement retry pod that carries the real XCom

evidence.excerpt: Maybe we should wrap it in a `while True` loop (+timeout) rather an if statment?

rule: Add new optional parameters to an existing provider hook or operator `__init__` as keyword-only arguments, placed after a `*` separator
trigger: A new optional parameter is inserted positionally into an existing `__init__` signature with no preceding `*` marker
rationale: Positional order carries no meaning for these configuration parameters, and keyword-only placement keeps the signature free to evolve without breaking existing callers

evidence.excerpt: order does not have any special meaning; keyword only arg would be better

rule: A provider hook/operator `:param:` docstring must describe the real runtime fallback and the real scope of validation — not the plausible-sounding one
trigger: A `:param X:` line claims a fallback such as "if None, the project ID from the connection is used" when the code passes `None` straight through, or a docstring summary claims to validate "format and existence" while only the format is checked
rationale: Provider docstrings are published as the user-facing API reference, so an invented default or validation claim misleads users configuring connections

evidence.excerpt: When quota_project_id is None, no quota project is configured at all
It doesn't validate existence (not sure that it should though)

rule: Check that an optional credential capability is callable with `callable(getattr(credentials, "with_quota_project", None))` rather than probing it with `hasattr`
trigger: `if not hasattr(credentials, "<method>")` guards a subsequent call to that method on a google-auth credentials object
rationale: `hasattr` only proves the attribute exists; a non-callable or `None` attribute then fails at the call site with a confusing error instead of the intended configuration error

evidence.excerpt: only verifies the attribute exists, not that it's callable

rule: When bumping the documented `api_version` example of a marketing-platform/Google operator, update the versioned API documentation URLs in the same docstring to match
trigger: A docstring's `:param api_version:` example changes (e.g. 'v4' to 'v5') while a "Check official API docs" link in the same class docstring still contains the old `/rest/v4/` segment
rationale: A version example and a doc link that disagree send users to the reference for an API version the operator no longer calls

evidence.excerpt: URL in the same docstring still points to /rest/v4/ — please update the referenced URLs

rule: Collapse provider unit tests that differ only in one input and one expected value into a single test using `@pytest.mark.parametrize`
trigger: Two adjacent test functions such as `test_x_with_<flag>` / `test_x_without_<flag>` share an identical body apart from one argument and one assertion
rationale: Near-duplicate hook tests drift apart when the hook changes; the parametrized form keeps the shared assertions in one place

evidence.excerpt: looks pretty similar, is there a chance to combine them with `@pytest.mark.parametrize`?

rule: A test for an error-suppression flag (`ignore_error`, soft-fail behaviour) must make the mocked client raise the real provider exception via `side_effect` and assert nothing propagates — asserting that the flag was forwarded is not coverage
trigger: A new test exercising `ignore_error=True` only asserts `<method>.assert_called_once_with(..., on_error=mock.ANY)` and never sets `side_effect`
rationale: Passthrough assertions leave the actual suppression path untested, so a regression in the error handler still ships green

evidence.excerpt: This test doesn't actually verify that the `ignore_error` flag works correctly

rule: Every public hook method added must get a unit test asserting the mocked client call chain arguments and the returned value, following the pattern already established in that test module
trigger: A hook gains public methods (e.g. `get_report`, `list_reports`) but the matching `providers/*/tests/unit/.../test_<hook>.py` only covers a subset of them
rationale: Discovery-API hooks are thin wrappers whose only real failure mode is wrong parameter names, so per-method call-chain assertions are the coverage that matters

evidence.excerpt: hook methods `get_report` and `list_reports` are missing test coverage

rule: Do not swallow credential-resolution or token-refresh failures inside a secrets backend; surface or chain the original error instead of letting it degrade into the backend's generic error
trigger: `except Exception: pass` (or an equally broad silent handler) wraps `credentials.refresh(...)` or a metadata-server lookup in a secrets backend or its internal client
rationale: Swallowed ADC failures resurface later as a generic VaultError about an expected string, which makes production authentication problems very hard to diagnose

evidence.excerpt: makes production ADC failures much harder to diagnose. Please preserve or surface the original error

rule: Resolve team-scoped secrets through the same `_get_team_or_global_secret` helper for connections, variables and config alike; do not gate it behind `conf.getboolean("core", "multi_team")`
trigger: A secrets backend getter branches on the `core.multi_team` config value to choose between the team-aware lookup and the plain lookup
rationale: The team-aware helper already falls back to the global path, so the extra config branch makes connection lookup behave differently from variable lookup for no reason

evidence.excerpt: Why cannot we do this regardless of whether multi team is configured? Same as variable

rule: Tests for behaviour gated on an Airflow config flag must cover the flag-off state as well, using `conf_vars` to assert the legacy path is unchanged
trigger: Every new test wraps the call in `with conf_vars({("core", "multi_team"): "True"})` and no test exercises the same call with the flag disabled
rationale: The disabled path is where truthy-string config bugs hide; without that case a regression that always applies the team prefix passes CI

evidence.excerpt: no regression test ensuring that when `core.multi_team` is disabled the team prefix is skipped

rule: Async notifier and async execution paths must go through the provider's hook rather than opening a raw client session such as `aiohttp.ClientSession()` inline
trigger: An `async def async_notify`/async execute path constructs `aiohttp.ClientSession()` directly instead of awaiting the provider's async hook method
rationale: Bypassing the hook discards connection lookup, auth and retry configuration; reviewers tolerate it only because a precedent exists and prefer refactoring the hook instead

evidence.excerpt: might be a better way so that we don't have to bypass the hook

rule: `ui-field-behaviour` placeholders in `provider.yaml` must be valid literal JSON that a user can paste straight into a Connection `extra` field — never Python expressions or attribute references
trigger: A `placeholders.extra` block in `provider.yaml` contains a non-JSON token such as `cls.default_open_options` or any other Python expression
rationale: The placeholder is rendered verbatim in the connection UI and copied by users, so anything that is not valid JSON becomes a runtime parsing failure in their deployment

evidence.excerpt: includes `cls.default_open_options`, which is not valid JSON and will be copied by users

rule: Regenerate the provider metadata (`get_provider_info.py`) in the same change whenever `provider.yaml` is edited
trigger: A diff touches a `provider.yaml` (connection types, ui-field-behaviour, extras) with no matching update to that provider's generated `get_provider_info.py`
rationale: The generated metadata is what Airflow reads at runtime, so leaving it stale makes the yaml and the shipped provider info disagree

evidence.excerpt: then regenerate provider metadata so `get_provider_info.py` stays consistent

rule: `get_conn()` must resolve connection-derived configuration into local variables and never overwrite attributes that were set in `__init__`
trigger: `get_conn()` assigns to `self.<param>` from `connection.extra_dejson` or a `getattr(..., default)` fallback chain
rationale: Hooks are reused and `get_conn()` can be called many times, so the first call permanently clobbers the value the user passed to the constructor with a defaulted one

evidence.excerpt: the first call permanently overwrites whatever was passed in `__init__`

rule: Centralize an optional provider SDK import in a single helper that raises `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException`, instead of repeating a bare in-method `import` that surfaces a raw `ImportError`
trigger: The same third-party SDK (e.g. `import ibmmq`) is imported inside several methods of a hook/operator with no shared helper and no optional-feature exception
rationale: Optional extras must fail with a clear user-facing message naming the extra to install, and a single import site stops the guard logic from drifting between methods

evidence.excerpt: these imports should fail with a clear, user-facing `AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException` rather than a raw `ImportError`
